source.title: SGD with a Constant Large Learning Rate Can Converge to Local Maxima
source.authors: Liu Ziyin; Botao Li; James B. Simon; Masakuni Ueda

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendices; no truncation or garbling that prevents extraction is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether SGD can converge to local maxima or saddle points, using constructed toy landscapes and a minimal neural-network-like example. Its results refine the broad training-success claim by showing failures under specific recipes and explicitly caution that the constructions are far from practice.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's own theoretical and experimental results about SGD convergence and its toy neural-network example. Statements about prior work are excluded. The paper also reports Adam and AMSGrad comparisons, but those optimizer comparisons do not test a listed claim version and are omitted.
record.test_reason: The study establishes worst-case behavior of constant-rate SGD on constructed objectives and a one-neuron quadratic-activation network. None of its results tests V1–V6. In particular, the learning-rate sweep does not measure recovery above an initial linearized stability threshold, curvature reduction, or full-batch edge-of-stability dynamics.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors show that constant-rate SGD can converge to maxima or saddles, escape arbitrarily slowly, and favor sharper minima in constructed examples. They explicitly describe the examples as far from practice and leave applicability to larger, deeper networks open.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses worst-case constructed scalar and two-dimensional objectives plus a minimal two-layer one-neuron network, rather than benchmark classification training from random initialization. Its learning rates are held constant in the main setting.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate changes the outcome in the toy neural-network example: λ=0.001 reaches the global-minimum valley, λ=0.1 converges to a saddle point, and divergence begins at about λ=0.11. The scalar examples also give explicit learning-rate regimes for convergence or escape.

fits_no_version.finding: A minimal quadratic-activation network reaches the global-minimum valley at learning rate 0.001, converges to a saddle in all 1000 runs at 0.1, and diverges above 0.108.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Constant-rate SGD can converge to a suboptimal saddle or diverge in a minimal nonlinear regression network, depending on learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Constructed scalar sampled objectives attract SGD to a local maximum under specified sampling and learning-rate conditions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: State-dependent minibatch noise can cause constant-rate SGD to converge to a local maximum.

fits_no_version.finding: For the constructed two-dimensional objective, suitable noise parameters force convergence, when it occurs, to sharper minima.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD need not prefer flatter minima in nonconvex objectives.

fits_no_version.finding: Proposition 3 and Appendix A.3 show that the optimal saddle escape rate can approach zero even after tuning the constant learning rate within λ ≤ 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Constructed objectives can make constant-rate SGD escape a specified saddle arbitrarily slowly despite learning-rate tuning.

record.problems: The authors characterize the constructed problems as minimal and simplistic toy examples far from practice. The neural-network demonstration has only two layers, one hidden neuron, a single data point, and an uncertain label; it uses MSE rather than classification. No results on CIFAR or other benchmark classification tasks are reported. The figure-based learning-rate sweep does not give exact interval endpoints in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows omitted; the study's other optimizer demonstrations (Adam and AMSGrad) do not bear on the listed versions of the claim.

untested.parts: Training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels and size or recipe dependence.
Spurious-local-minimum frequency and the benefit of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-dependent training degradation, identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization or normalization exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, training speed, and trainable depth.
Recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, transient loss and curvature dynamics, full-batch sharpness thresholds, and divergence relative to those thresholds.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup's comparable training without normalization.

record.verdict_notes: The extracted rows describe real findings, but their states cannot be interpreted as evidence for any supplied version. Citations to memorization and large-learning-rate work do not make the study a test of V1 or V5.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, classification error, large convolutional networks, corrupted or random labels, and model size are not tested.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student problem, teacher/student width sweep, or spurious-local-minimum frequency is tested.
No depth sweep, plain versus residual shortcut comparison, batch normalization comparison, or ImageNet/CIFAR classification training is tested.
No activation-matched initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian comparison, or depth sweep is tested.
The study does not test training above a linearized stability limit, curvature dynamics, sharpness thresholds, or the stated wide-network squared-loss conditions.
No batch-normalization versus no-normalization comparison, accuracy-speed comparison, or higher-learning-rate tolerance comparison is tested.

rows.subject: SGD on quadratic loss L̂(w)=xw²/2
rows.operation_detail: Proposition 1 analyzes SGD with λ=1 and a two-point sample distribution; parameters converge to the local maximum.

conditions.value: x = 1 and x = −1 + a with equal probability; a < 0

rows.value: w converges to w = 0 with probability 1
rows.note: The result concerns a constructed scalar objective, not classification error or a benchmark network.
rows.check: The reported convergence is correctly extracted, but it measures no listed version. The subject is a constructed scalar objective, not a neural network.

rows.subject: SGD on quadratic loss L̂(w)=xw²/2
rows.operation_detail: Proposition 2 gives a condition for SGD to converge in probability to the local maximum.
rows.value: SGD converges to the local maximum in probability if µ < 0
rows.note: The proposition states a theoretical result for a scalar quadratic sampled loss.
rows.check: The convergence condition measures no listed version. Specify negative expected x so that zero is a local maximum; μ < 0 alone establishes attraction to zero, not its classification as a maximum. The subject is a scalar objective.

rows.subject: SGD on quadratic loss L̂(w)=xw²/2
rows.operation_detail: Corollary 1 characterizes a learning-rate interval where the scalar SGD process converges to the local maximum.
rows.measure: Convergence in probability to the local maximum
rows.value: SGD converges to the local maximum in probability within the stated interval
rows.note: A constructed scalar loss and specified two-point sampling distribution.
rows.check: The interval measures no listed version. Include a < 0 for the local-maximum interpretation. The subject is a scalar objective.

rows.subject: SGD on two-dimensional fourth-order loss L̂(w₁,w₂)
rows.operation_detail: Proposition 4 proves that, for a constructed loss and suitable b, convergence in probability implies convergence to one of the sharper minima.

conditions.value: λ < c for some constant c = O(1)
there exists b such that if SGD converges in probability

rows.value: converges to the sharper minimum at (w₁,w₂) = (0, ±√((1+a)/2))
rows.note: The proposition is conditional on convergence and a suitable b; it does not establish benchmark classification behavior.
rows.check: Preference for sharper minima measures no listed version, including V5's sharpness dynamics relative to a stability threshold. This is a constructed two-dimensional objective; retain the conditional nature of the proposition.

rows.subject: SGD on two-layer one-neuron neural network f(x)=w₂σ(w₁x), σ(x)=x²
rows.operation_detail: Learning rate varied and average stationary training loss measured.

conditions.value: w₁ uniform in [−1,1]; w₂ uniform in [0,1]

rows.value: For a significant range of large learning rates, models converge to a saddle point with L = 2.5; divergence at λ ≈ 0.11
rows.note: The reported sweep demonstrates both saddle convergence and divergence in this toy network; the text gives no exact endpoints for the large-rate interval.
rows.check: The sweep measures no listed version, so partial is not a version-relative state. Figure 3 explicitly reports divergence for learning rates larger than 0.108; the record's statement that the text supplies no precise threshold should be corrected.
